initial_requirements: The Mars Express ASPERA-3 science team needs a ground data system that processes and preserves telemetry from the mission's particle and field instruments. The facility should acquire incoming spacecraft data, transform it into products suitable for scientific analysis, distribute those products to the project team, and provide recent information for public viewing. Validated products must also be retained and delivered for long-term scientific archiving.

messages.content: Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the ASPERA-3 Processing and Archiving Facility so we can understand the needed functionality clearly. Before we begin, are you in line with the scope of this interview, or do your expectations differ?

Yes, I’m aligned with that scope. I’m here to discuss the ground data system for acquiring ASPERA-3 telemetry, processing it into science-ready products, distributing those products to the team, showing recent public information, and preserving validated data for long-term archiving.
Thank you. To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m speaking as a representative of the ASPERA-3 science team and the operations side of the project. My focus is on making sure the facility supports our data processing, distribution, and archiving needs for the mission instruments.
Thank you. Could you describe the current process or system you use today for receiving, processing, distributing, and archiving ASPERA-3 telemetry?

At the moment, the flow is fairly manual and spread across a few separate tools and scripts. We receive the spacecraft telemetry, run processing to turn it into usable science products, then distribute those products to the team and set aside validated data for archive delivery. The biggest pain points are keeping the steps consistent and making sure the preserved products are tracked cleanly over the long term.
What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what are the main features you hope to get from this project?

We want to automate and standardize as much of the ingest and processing chain as possible, so we’re not relying on people to move files around or rerun steps by hand. We also need more reliable product distribution to the science team, better visibility into recent data for public access, and a cleaner path from validated products into long-term archive packages. Ideally the facility will reduce operational overhead and make the data flow much more traceable.

So the main features/functions you want are automated and standardized ingest and processing, reliable product distribution to the science team, public access to recent data, and a cleaner archive packaging and delivery path for validated products, correct?
Yes, that’s correct. Those are the main capabilities we’re looking for, along with traceability so we can tell what was processed, when, and whether it was validated and delivered successfully.
Are there any other features you would like to see in this project, perhaps something that has not been the primary focus so far?

One thing we’d value is good monitoring and reporting, so operators can quickly see if a processing run failed or if a delivery to the archive is pending. It would also be helpful to have consistent metadata handling across all products, since that affects both science use and archive quality. I don’t think those are separate headline goals, but they’re important supporting features.
Based on your description, do you think automated monitoring and reporting for processing and delivery status, plus consistent metadata handling across all products, should also be included?
Yes, I think they should be included. They’re not just nice to have; they support the core workflow and help us trust the outputs, so they belong in the facility requirements.
